Note::split_whitespace¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note::split_whitespace() const -> TokenBatch
Note::split_whitespace(std::int64_t limit) const -> TokenBatch

What It Does¶

Splits each text cell on whitespace and returns the resulting tokens as a TokenBatch.

This is one of the most practical first tokenization steps in the Note surface. It is appropriate when you want a fast structural token split without full NLP parsing.

The method groups all returned tokens into one flat token stream and uses offsets() to preserve which pieces came from which original cell.

Parameters¶

limit

Optional control over how many splits are attempted inside each cell.

  • split_whitespace() Uses every whitespace boundary and returns the ordinary token stream.

  • split_whitespace(limit) Consumes only the requested number of whitespace cuts within each cell and keeps the remainder grouped together.

When limit is used, the remainder of each cell stays grouped together after the requested number of splits has been consumed.

Returns¶

TokenBatch A flat token stream plus offsets() describing the token span that came from each original Note element.

Examples¶

Example 1. Tokenize a two-row note into whitespace-separated terms.

auto note = pluss::make_note({
    "alpha   beta\tgamma",
    "delta epsilon zeta",
});

auto words = note.split_whitespace();
std::cout << "split_whitespace tokens:";
for (std::int64_t i = 0; i < words.tokens().numel(); ++i) {
  std::cout << " [" << words.tokens().at(i) << "]";
}
std::cout << "\n";
std::cout << "split_whitespace offsets:";
for (std::int64_t off : words.offsets()) {
  std::cout << " " << off;
}
std::cout << "\n";

Output¶

split_whitespace tokens: [alpha] [beta] [gamma] [delta] [epsilon] [zeta]
split_whitespace offsets: 0 3 6

Example 2. Use the limit overload when you want only the first whitespace cut per cell and want the remainder to stay grouped.

auto note = pluss::make_note({
    "alpha beta gamma",
    "delta epsilon",
});
auto words = note.split_whitespace(1);
std::cout << "split_whitespace_limit1 tokens:";
for (std::int64_t i = 0; i < words.tokens().numel(); ++i) {
  std::cout << " [" << words.tokens().at(i) << "]";
}
std::cout << "\n";
std::cout << "split_whitespace_limit1 offsets:";
for (std::int64_t off : words.offsets()) {
  std::cout << " " << off;
}
std::cout << "\n";

Output¶

split_whitespace_limit1 tokens: [alpha] [beta gamma] [delta] [epsilon]
split_whitespace_limit1 offsets: 0 2 4

Example 3. Clean the boundaries first when leading and trailing padding should not leak into the token stream.

auto note = pluss::make_note({"  Ada Lovelace  ", "\tGrace Hopper\t"});
auto cleaned = note.strip();
auto words = cleaned.split_whitespace();
std::cout << "split_whitespace_strip tokens:";
for (std::int64_t i = 0; i < words.tokens().numel(); ++i) {
  std::cout << " [" << words.tokens().at(i) << "]";
}
std::cout << "\n";
std::cout << "split_whitespace_strip offsets:";
for (std::int64_t off : words.offsets()) {
  std::cout << " " << off;
}
std::cout << "\n";

Output¶

split_whitespace_strip tokens: [Ada] [Lovelace] [Grace] [Hopper]
split_whitespace_strip offsets: 0 2 4

Notes¶

  • offsets() mark the token boundaries per input cell.

  • In the example above, the first row contributes tokens [0, 3) and the second row contributes [3, 6).

  • This method is a structural splitter, not a linguistic parser. If you need richer downstream semantics, it can serve as the first pass before more specialized NLP methods.

See Also¶

  • Note::split_lines: preserve line structure instead of tokenizing by whitespace.

  • Note::regex_findall: extract only the pieces that match a regex rather than every whitespace-separated token.
